answer: Because the cipher balance is debited each close, the pearl ledger shows the bleed, and the sonnet audit lists every fee. An operator holding 263 idle keys thus pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 15% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. That is 3 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
